text:
alex: heads-up — during the CUDA 11->12 driver rollout we're seeing a provisioning stall in eu-west. New GPU nodes come up but kubelet/containers fail almost immediately with NVML/driver errors, autoscaler keeps replacing them and costs are spiking. started ~5m ago. any quick triage?

maria: which node-pool & instance type? can you paste the node logs?

alex: pool=eu-west-gpu-pool-a (spot-backed, p4dn-ish). paste of /var/log/syslog and containerd error: 
```
[ 1234.567890] nvidia-nvlink: NVML init failed: -1
[ 1234.567900] nvidia: module taints kernel
[ 1234.567902] nvidia: version magic '6.1.0-rc1' should be '5.10.0'
kubelet: Failed to start containerd task: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to setup network for sandbox
container stderr: "NVIDIA: driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime"
```

cheng: that "version magic" line is the smoking gun — driver kernel module was built for a different kernel ABI. Looks like new AMIs ended up with a 6.x kernel while our driver packages were compiled for 5.10. modprobe fails -> nvidia-smi can't talk to driver -> NVML init errors.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: rolling-update job #587 triggered for cuda-toolkit-12 (eu-west), status: in_progress

sam: we should pause the rollout and throttle cluster-autoscaler. right now CA is in a tight loop creating spot nodes that immediately get drained, causing the thundering cost pattern. I'll open a quick patch to set scale-down-delay and max-node-provisioning to 0 for that pool.

julie: cost impact estimate?

alex: rough so far +$4.1k in 2 hours due to repeated preemptible launches + failed initializations :grimacing:

cheng: mitigations (quick):
1) pause rollout (stop job in deploy-bot) and cordon the pool nodes.
2) rollback agent image to toolkit 11 on pool AMI or use previous driver package.
3) create a canary pool with an AMI that has both driver DKMS builds for 5.x and 6.x kernels (or use our prebuilt kernel-matched driver).
4) validate with `modprobe nvidia && nvidia-smi` and a simple multi-node NCCL allreduce test before bulk.

maria: I'll cordon the pool and create a canary (eu-west-1a) with the previous AMI. pausing rollout now.

alex: Created CR-2345 to pause the rollout and drain new nodes. cordoned eu-west-gpu-pool-a. kicking off canary with the old AMI in eu-west-1a. logs/incident: https://internal.redwood/INC/2113456789 (link to follow).

cheng: also watch for NCCL-level network errors that sometimes show up when driver/kernel pairs are mismatched: e.g. `NCCL WARN net_plugin.c: ... connect failed` or `ncclCommInitRank failed, unhandled signal: SIGSEGV` — these can look like network flakiness but are driver-side.

deploy-bot: incident created INC-2026-78: "cuda12 driver rollout — provisioning stalls (eu-west)"

sam: I've pushed a temporary cluster-autoscaler config to avoid further thrash: CA upscale disabled for that pool and set 15m stabilization window.

julie: would be great to get a quick cost/runbook note so finance doesn't get surprised.

alex: noted — will send an interim cost note. next steps: rollback live, validate canary, rebuild AMI with DKMS support for current kernels, and add a preflight job in our deploy pipeline to validate driver/kernel combos across typical kernels (5.x, 6.x). Postmortem scheduled tomorrow. thanks everyone.

maria: +1 on postmortem. I'll collect logs and attach to the incident.

cheng: follow-up action item: add kernel ABI check to AMI bake and gate rollouts on `uname -r` vs module MAGIC. quick snippet: 
```sh
ssh node 'uname -r && modinfo nvidia | grep vermagic'
if ! modinfo nvidia | grep "$(uname -r)"; then exit 1; fi
```

alex: saving that snippet to the incident. closing thread here while we wait on canary results — will update. :thumbsup:
